papers.title: EDGAR: Efficient Diffusion-Driven Gaussian Avatar Refinement via Synthetic Failure

summary.tldr: EDGAR uses a one-step Mixture-of-Experts diffusion model trained on a novel synthetic failure dataset to refine monocular Gaussian avatar renderings while maintaining identity and temporal consistency.
key_points: Constructs EDGAR-SET, a hybrid triplet dataset pairing degraded Gaussian renderings with ground-truth and reference images to simulate realistic avatar failures.
Integrates a fusion block that feeds self-supervised Sapiens identity features into a one-step Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) diffusion backbone to handle varied artifact types efficiently.
Applies refined multi-view outputs as pseudo-targets to re-optimize the single underlying Gaussian avatar, avoiding the need for per-frame diffusion inference during final rendering.
Demonstrates improved perceptual, reconstruction, and cross-view calibrated consistency metrics over raw outputs and SDEdit baselines across three avatar reconstruction methods.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables high-quality, artifact-free 3D head avatar rendering by using diffusion refinement strictly during the offline training phase without incurring inference-time latency.

papers.title: Terminal-style Mathematical Modeling Bench: The First Agentic and Verifiable Benchmark for Mathematical Modeling

summary.tldr: TB-MathModel is the first agentic, containerized benchmark for complete contest-style mathematical modeling, using programmatic validation and multi-reference scoring to verifiably evaluate model solutions against human Outstanding papers.
key_points: Evaluates agents on 18 real CUMCM and MCM problems (2023–2025) provided with verbatim statements, attachments, and figures in a containerized terminal environment.
Employs a two-layer feasibility verification system featuring programmatic gates for six decidable invariant forms and 624 Lean 4 obligations that zero out infeasible answers.
Uses direction-aware, one-sided scoring that compares model outputs against a panel of human Outstanding-award papers without penalizing superior performance.
Benchmarked seven multimodal systems, with the top model achieving a 64.58% multi-reference O-Eval score and an open model reaching 59.81% at 1/100th of the cost.
summary.why_it_matters: It establishes a machine-checkable, hard-gated benchmark that eliminates reliance on subjective LLM judges for open-ended, long-horizon mathematical modeling tasks.

papers.title: Future Representation Distillation for Imagination-free World Action Models

summary.tldr: DreamFree is a World Action Model that distillates predictive visual representations from a frozen video diffusion model using only current observations, enabling 11Hz real-time robot control without generating future video frames.
key_points: Repurposes a pretrained video diffusion model as a predictive visual encoder via representation distillation from single-frame observations.
Trains an action module on the distilled representations to extract action-relevant information without iterative video denoising or future video generation.
Operates real-time closed-loop control at 11Hz using a 14B parameter video diffusion backbone.
Enables task learning from unannotated video demonstrations, including cross-embodiment transfers, and scales performance with larger video priors and dataset sizes.
summary.why_it_matters: It eliminates the latency and visual inaccuracy bottlenecks of video-generation-based robot control, allowing real-time execution of video-diffusion-powered action models.

papers.title: From Autonomous Agents to Cognitive Symbionts: Toward AI-Augmented Human Intelligence

summary.tldr: This paper introduces AI-Augmented Human Intelligence (AHI) and proposes cognitive symbionts—lifelong, embedded, proactive AI systems designed to bridge the cognitive gap between a person's potential knowledge and their working memory capacity.
key_points: Defines the cognitive gap as the difference between what a person could bring to a situation and what they can actively maintain in working memory.
Outlines a symbiosis loop design space comprising sensing, keeping, understanding, living alongside, acting for, thinking with, and growing alongside the user.
Requires a personal runtime framework governed by trust to deliver real-time, low-friction, proactive, and private assistance.
Identifies unique societal risks stemming from augmented human capabilities, including covert examination assistance and social pressure to adopt AHI systems.
summary.why_it_matters: AHI shifts the paradigm from autonomous systems that replace human effort to embedded, continuous AI that directly expands individual human cognitive capacity.

papers.title: Decode Before You Hear: Speculative Listening for Chunk-Interleaved Full-Duplex Speech Language Models

summary.tldr: Speculative Listening is a training-free, lossless self-speculative decoding framework that utilizes idle compute during input time to accelerate chunk-interleaved full-duplex speech language models.
key_points: Empirical analysis showed the next audio chunk leaves output unchanged in 95.3% of chunks, and 88% of changes originate at the first output token.
During idle time while awaiting audio, the model drafts the next chunk assuming silence, plus a secondary branch from the runner-up first token if changes occur.
Drafts are stored in a cross-chunk hypothesis pool and verified instantly once real audio arrives.
Achieves 2.6-2.8x speedup on speak chunks, up to 23.4x on tool-call chunks, a 73% reduction in response start delay (down to 74-241 ms), and a 94.4% drop in maximum real-time lag on TickTock-Bench.
summary.why_it_matters: It drastically reduces response latencies in full-duplex speech language models to human-like turn-taking speeds without requiring model retraining or sacrificing output quality.

papers.title: Muir: Linear Attention with Sensitivity-Allocated Gating and Matched-Filter Readout

summary.tldr: Muir optimizes linear attention by pairing sensitivity-allocated low-rank gate projections with matched-filter readout, outperforming Gated DeltaNet-2 and standard Transformers.
key_points: Identifies an asymmetry in state updates: key normalization concentrates energy onto sparse channels (allowing lower-rank erase gates), whereas value writes scale all channels.
Introduces matched-filter readout gating to re-weight slow- and fast-decaying state rows, preventing unweighted state rows from dominating outputs and reducing the need for aggressive erasure.

Fuses gating into a sensitivity-allocated low-rank projection, reinvesting saved parameters into a wider feed-forward network, supported by a novel chunkwise parallel update algorithm for stable training.

Demonstrates performance gains across 166M–1.34B parameter scales, including 1.8–2.0% lower perplexity over GDN-2, near-100% passkey retrieval up to 1M tokens, and 2,560x length extrapolation to 10M-token streams.
summary.why_it_matters: Muir delivers superior long-context reasoning, recall, and perplexity while training 2.7x faster than Transformers at 32K context lengths without incurring inference memory overhead.

papers.title: SwarmEvolve: Latent Agent Swarms for Evolutionary Discovery and Optimization

summary.tldr: SwarmEvolve accelerates program optimization by executing swarms of low-cost agents that reason and exchange crossover ideas entirely within latent space via KV cache sharing.
key_points: Replaces text decoding with latent space reasoning and KV cache passing across hundreds of concurrent agents per round.
Implements a novelty filter that selects diverse agent ideas by computing distances between their hidden state vectors.
Performs latent crossover by using a summarizer agent that ingests combined KV caches from multiple swarm members.
Achieves target state-of-the-art solution scores in a median of 3 to 8 minutes compared to 60 minutes for baseline frameworks across 21 benchmarks.
Outperforms prior solutions discovered by AlphaEvolve using a smaller Qwen3 8B model.
summary.why_it_matters: Communicating directly via latent space and KV caches drastically lowers the computational cost and time required for LLM-driven evolutionary program search.

papers.title: Towards Real-Time Full-Waveform LiDAR Transformers via Intensity-Guided Token Reduction and Physics-Aware Augmentation

summary.tldr: FWL-ToPM and FWLAug introduce intensity-guided token reduction and physics-aware data augmentation to enable the first real-time, high-accuracy Transformer for Full-Waveform LiDAR.
key_points: FWL-ToPM uses intensity distributions to prune and merge redundant low-intensity background tokens, achieving over an 8x speedup at real-time throughput.
FWLAug acts as a regularization method by preserving the Time-of-Flight ray waveforms and frustum geometry during data augmentation.
Evaluated on the Ghost-FWL benchmark, the approach achieves a nearly 9-point F1 score improvement over prior state-of-the-art methods while enhancing performance on unseen out-of-distribution scenes.
summary.why_it_matters: It overcomes high computational costs and data scarcity in Full-Waveform LiDAR perception, enabling real-time deployment on autonomous vehicles operating in adverse environmental conditions.

papers.title: Reducing Representational Interference in Retrieval Embeddings with Trainable Prefix Tokens

summary.tldr: Prepending trainable [DUMP] tokens to input sequences during contrastive embedding training reduces representational interference from low-information tokens without modifying model architecture, loss functions, or pooling strategies.
key_points: Prepends trainable [DUMP] prefix tokens to inputs, which are optimized via standard contrastive retrieval objectives.
Absorbs residual token-level artifacts and uninformative signals, including attention sink behavior, away from the final pooling representation.
Alters token-level activation and attention patterns of low-information tokens during encoding.
Demonstrates consistent retrieval performance gains over finetuned baselines across both encoder and decoder embedding architectures on long-context benchmarks.
summary.why_it_matters: It offers a lightweight, architectural-change-free method to improve text embedding quality by isolating uninformative token noise during dense retrieval fine-tuning.

papers.title: StepX-OPD: Rethinking Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation in Diffusion Models

summary.tldr: StepX-OPD unifies multi-teacher capability consolidation and few-step distillation into a single stage, enabling diffusion models to learn multiple capabilities in a few steps while outperforming multi-step teachers.
key_points: Merges capability integration and step reduction into one phase where frozen specialist teachers supervise student rollouts on actual visited states.
Regresses the student's velocity on the low-noise segment of the rollout, addressing KL decomposition findings that weight velocity mismatch heaviest near the clean image end.
Mitigates unintended text generation caused by capability integration using a specialized variant.
Outperforms the 40-step Flow-OPD baseline using 4-step sampling on SD3.5-Medium and FLUX.1-dev across instruction following, text rendering, and human preference metrics.
Reduces training compute on SD3.5-Medium by approximately 37% GPU-hours compared to sequential DiffusionOPD and step distillation.
summary.why_it_matters: It eliminates the performance degradation and GPU-hour overhead of sequential diffusion model compression by training fast, few-step models directly from specialized full-step teachers.

papers.title: Multi-layer Indexer: Overlapping Selection and Attention in DeepSeek Sparse Attention

summary.tldr: Multi-layer Indexer (MLI) eliminates DeepSeek Sparse Attention's indexer bottleneck by running each layer's indexer concurrently with attention using the previous layer's selection, requiring no retraining, new weights, or extra kernels.
key_points: Exploits token selection overlap between adjacent layers to let a layer attend to the previous indexer's selected k=2048 tokens, running the current indexer scan in parallel.
Integrates directly into SGLang's production decode graph without model retraining, with an optional fused decode kernel for DeepSeek-V3.2.
Composes with IndexCache (IndexShare in GLM-5.2) to hide indexer scan overhead on layers that retain indexers across retention ratios from 1/2 to 1/32 and contexts up to 195K.

Delivers up to 14.5% faster decoding on DeepSeek-V3.2 and 9.8% on GLM-5 over IndexCache at 1/2 retention, reaching 1.32x base throughput at 1/4 retention on 128K context while maintaining accuracy on LongBench, RULER, and LongBench v2.
summary.why_it_matters: MLI significantly speeds up long-context LLM inference for architectures like DeepSeek-V3.2 and GLM-5 by overlapping indexer computation with attention, outperforming prior layer-dropping methods without degrading accuracy.

papers.title: Information Games: Strategic Crowding and Firm Repositioning in Language-Model Space

summary.tldr: Researchers developed a model of costly competitive adjustment and a novel sandwich estimator to analyze how firms strategically reallocate capacity in response to cash flow shocks, validating it via vector-based representations of corporate news.
key_points: Models competitive capacity adjustments and firm repositioning in response to discounted free cash flow shocks based on the theoretical framework of Xu et al. (2022).
Uses LLM-based search engine embeddings to convert corporate news and analyst reports into dense vector clouds that capture changes in information geometry and firm dissimilarity over time.
Introduces a novel sandwich estimator applied within multi-agent simulations to evaluate the sign and magnitude of predicted firm capacity adjustments.
Validates the model empirical predictions using news and analyst reports from Nasdaq-listed companies covering the 2018–2022 period.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates how dense vector representations generated by language models can be used to track corporate strategic adjustments and quantify competitive crowding in market ecosystems.

papers.title: TaoMate-HD: Progressive-Resolution Autoregressive Audio-Video Generation

summary.tldr: TaoMate-HD is an autoregressive streaming audio-video framework that uses a progressive-resolution multi-step trajectory, history-passing across chunks, and asymmetric text continuation training for high-resolution digital human generation.
key_points: Processes video in short chunks using two low-resolution denoising steps for coarse structure followed by a final high-resolution refinement step, generating synchronized audio alongside.
Passes audiovisual predictions from each stage to the corresponding stage of the next chunk as history, preserving state across text updates to prevent speech repetition or interruption.
Uses asymmetric text continuation training with separate text windows dedicated to generation and distillation, reducing character error rate by 11.18 percentage points over the baseline.

Achieves a 1.6x speedup over direct high-resolution generation, with optimized stage-parallel deployment yielding an additional 1.9x overall speedup over serial execution while supporting hour-long generation.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables efficient, real-time, high-resolution digital human audio-video streaming without speech artifacts during dynamic text updates.

papers.title: Ask, Don't Equip: Question-Driven Coding Agents for Deep Kernel Optimization

summary.tldr: KernelSeek uses question-driven prompts instead of complex tools or fixed scripts to optimize CUDA kernels, outperforming FlashAttention-3 and FlashAttention-4.
key_points: KernelSeek relies on a minimal harness enforcing verifiable goals combined with human- and self-applied question banks at decision points.
Achieved 1.13x FlashAttention-3 performance where a tool-rich autonomous agent plateaued at 0.50x after 133 steps.
Generated standalone, dependency-free CUDA forward kernels without CUTLASS, CuTe, cuBLAS, or cuDNN.
Attained geometric mean speedups of 1.16x over FlashAttention-3 on Hopper and 1.46x over FlashAttention-4 on Blackwell across 182 scenarios per architecture.
Analysis of 162 human messages and 11.5K agent tool calls showed major performance gains resulted from questions shifting systemic focus or challenging claimed limits, rather than injected facts.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that targeted, directional questioning is more effective for LLM-based GPU kernel optimization than equipping agents with heavy external toolsets and libraries.

papers.title: Signed but Steerable: Measuring and Closing the Text-Vector Integrity Gap in Offline Retrieval-Augmented Generation

summary.tldr: Researchers identify a security vulnerability in offline RAG systems where signed precomputed vectors can be manipulated independently of text, and propose a deterministic code-verification method to restore text-vector integrity.
key_points: Offline RAG knowledge packs introduce a text-vector integrity gap where cryptographic signatures verify the publisher but do not guarantee vectors match their corresponding text.

Using cosine tolerance verifiers fails: calibrating tolerances to CPU INT8-FP32 variance leaves 98-100% of queries vulnerable to vector hijacking, reducing Raspberry Pi 5 LLM accuracy from 0.75 to 0.39.
Auditing compressed vector stores is ineffective; tampered vectors passing FAISS product-quantization audits ranked the attacker's document first in 25% of target queries across 57,638 documents.
Common floating-point and dynamic-INT8 inference pipelines lack bit-reproducibility across different batch sizes and hardware architectures.
Verifying quantization codes using verifier-side ambiguity resolution, canonicalization, and a calibrated guard band accepted all honest vectors while preventing unauthorized vector steering.
summary.why_it_matters: Accepting precomputed embeddings based on standard signatures or cosine tolerances allows malicious publishers to hijack RAG retrieval results on edge devices without altering the visible text.

papers.title: Can an LLM Actually Reason and Program about Neural Network's Weights or is it just memorization on steroids? Exploring "Weight-Space Programming"

summary.tldr: An evaluation of Claude Opus 5.5 reveals zero-shot weight reading of small CNNs relies on local arithmetic and memorized dataset priors rather than actual weight-flow tracing.
key_points: Evaluated Claude Opus 5.5 on 125,000-parameter CNNs given only raw plain-text weights without tools, dataset names, or forward passes.
The model performs accurate local calculations, such as inferring optimizer step counts from batch-normalization statistics and recovering label splits from output-layer sign patterns.
Semantic interpretations rely heavily on memorized priors, misidentifying fast-food, KMNIST, and SAT-6 datasets as CIFAR-10 or MNIST, and failing when label indices are permuted.
The model relies on reading initial and final layers while sampling middle layers, causing claims based on partial tracing to fail verification.
summary.why_it_matters: The findings demonstrate that current LLM weight-space programming capabilities are driven by local arithmetic and dataset memorization rather than true internal weight-flow reasoning.

papers.title: Circe: Training-Free LLM Self-Evaluation via Component Interaction Consistency

summary.tldr: Circe is a training-free LLM self-evaluation method that assesses response correctness without reference answers by combining internal model interaction signals with external output confidence.
key_points: Introduces Component Interaction Consistency (CIC) to measure directional alignment between early-layer attention updates and later-layer attention-induced FFN output changes.
Utilizes Representation Geometry (RG) to capture normalized displacement and angular changes in layerwise hidden-state trajectories.
Integrates Likelihood Confidence (LC), derived from the mean negative log-likelihood of generated tokens, as an external output signal.
Fuses CIC, RG, and LC into a single unified correctness score without requiring training data or repeated sampling.
Evaluated across five LLMs and six benchmarks spanning multilingual, multimodal, and open-world domains.
summary.why_it_matters: Circe enables reliable, training-free evaluation of LLM response correctness in real-world deployment settings where ground-truth reference answers are unavailable.

papers.title: Unpacking the Compute Efficiency of Strong-to-Weak OPD against GRPO

summary.tldr: Strong-to-weak on-policy distillation using external post-trained teachers is less compute-efficient than GRPO, but distilling a student's own GRPO expert checkpoints achieves target accuracy with up to 50x fewer distillation FLOPs.
key_points: Vanilla reverse-KL OPD using an external post-trained teacher achieves lower accuracy per training FLOP than GRPO and frequently causes response-length inflation.
Distilling a student's own GRPO checkpoint allows OPD to match that checkpoint's math accuracy using 50x fewer FLOPs than GRPO required to reach it.

Multi-teacher OPD consolidates per-domain GRPO experts into a single student matching expert accuracy, requiring distillation compute equal to just 5.2% (2 domains) and 8.0% (4 domains) of specialist training FLOPs.
The combined specialist training and multi-teacher distillation pipeline beats joint multi-domain GRPO performance while reducing total compute by 42.0%.
summary.why_it_matters: Using self-GRPO checkpoints and multi-teacher OPD drastically lowers the compute required to combine domain-specific expert capabilities into a single competitive model.

papers.title: Spectral and Subspace Dynamics of LoRA in Supervised Fine-Tuning and Reinforcement Learning

summary.tldr: Analysis of LoRA dynamics reveals that group-mean baseline subtraction in RL concentrates singular spectra and accelerates subspace rotation compared to SFT, enabling tailored spectral-flattening interventions that improve performance in both stages.
key_points: Tracking singular spectra and subspaces reveals RL concentrates the singular spectrum across all learning rates, whereas SFT expands it at moderate learning rates.
RL rotates singular subspaces significantly faster than SFT at lower learning rates.

A quadratic multi-index model identifies group-mean baseline subtraction as the single driver altering the balance between coherent fitting and gradient noise, which forces a lower risk-favorable learning rate in RL.

Stage-specific LoRA modifications were derived: SFT benefits from flattening the full update spectrum, while RL benefits from flattening the update spectrum outside the current LoRA increment span to accelerate subspace rotation.
summary.why_it_matters: Understanding the distinct mathematical dynamics between SFT and RL allows practitioners to optimize LoRA hyperparameters and update mechanisms specifically tailored for each tuning stage.

papers.title: Muir: Linear Attention with Sensitivity-Allocated Gating and Matched-Filter Readout

summary.tldr: Muir enhances linear attention by introducing sensitivity-allocated low-rank gating, matched-filter state readout, and a numerically stable parallel update algorithm for large chunk sizes.
key_points: Identifies an asymmetry where linear attention state updates are less sensitive to erasure than writes, allowing lower-rank parameterization for erase gates.
Fuses all gates into a low-rank projection and introduces a matched-filter readout gate to re-weight state rows according to their decay-dependent norms.
Reinvests saved parameters into a wider feed-forward network and uses a novel parallel update algorithm to prevent numerical instability in large chunkwise training.

Outperforms Gated DeltaNet-2 (GDN-2) with 1.8-2.0% lower perplexity, trains 2.7x faster than Transformer at 32K context, and extrapolates from 4K training context up to 10M tokens without perplexity drift.
summary.why_it_matters: Muir enables scalable linear-attention models to achieve superior long-context retention and lower perplexity than Transformers while maintaining fast, constant-memory inference.

papers.title: StrataFlux: Memory-Hierarchy-Native Low-Bit LLM Inference

summary.tldr: StrataFlux is an LLM inference framework that recovers accuracy lost in 2-4-bit weight and 2-3-bit KV-cache quantization by selectively streaming refinement precision from host RAM and SSDs without stalling generation.
key_points: Co-designs refinement representation, selection, and delivery to stream precision from off-GPU memory, overlapping transfers with computation and reusing fetched precision across decoding steps.
Reduces 2-bit Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct weight perplexity on WikiText-2 from 9.46 to 8.40 on an RTX 5090 while retaining 95.4% of the quantized baseline's throughput.
Increases Qwen3-8B accuracy on AIME 2024/2025 from 11.0% to 47.1% using 2-bit weights and 2-bit KV cache without increasing GPU memory consumption.
Matches the perplexity and generation speed of vLLM (using 4-bit AWQ weights and 8-bit KV) on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct at 128K context while utilizing roughly half the GPU memory.
summary.why_it_matters: It breaks the hardware memory ceiling for LLM inference, enabling low-bit quantized models to achieve high-precision accuracy levels using secondary host storage without suffering typical offloading latency penalties.

papers.title: FewStepRL: Fine-tuning Few-step Diffusion Models with Reinforcement Learning

summary.tldr: FewStepRL adapts reinforcement learning post-training objectives to few-step diffusion models using a systematic three-phase framework consisting of transformation, decomposition, and adaptation.
key_points: Transformation converts objectives over densities, velocities, or rewards into x-space policy predictions at the clean end or at explicitly marked transition levels.
Decomposition expresses the gradient of each objective as a combination of self-regression toward a reference anchor and a reward augmentation.
Adaptation derives anchors from the few-step model along its tangent or transport end, recovering instantaneous velocity directly from the main network or an auxiliary network.
Unified few-step versions of FlowGRPO, AWM, DiffusionNFT, DiffusionOPSD, and ReFL were derived within a single modular codebase.

Differentiable reward gradients proved most effective when affordable, while DiffusionNFT variants excelled for non-differentiable rewards; extra inference steps provided no systematic overall benefit.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables computationally efficient RL fine-tuning of diffusion models by overcoming the math mismatch between standard many-step RL objectives and few-step interval-velocity models.

papers.title: SwarmEvolve: Latent Agent Swarms for Evolutionary Discovery and Optimization

summary.tldr: SwarmEvolve accelerates program optimization by using hundreds of low-cost agents per round that reason and combine ideas directly in latent space via KV-cache passing.
key_points: Replaces textual chain-of-thought generation with latent-space reasoning to remove repetitive text decoding bottlenecks.
Shares ideas and executes natural crossover across swarm members by passing KV caches to a summarizer agent.
Applies a novelty filter that selects distinct agent ideas by calculating distances between hidden state vectors.
Achieves top scores across 21 math and scientific computing problems, reaching state-of-the-art 60-minute baselines in a median of 3 to 8 minutes using Qwen3 8B.
summary.why_it_matters: Communicating through latent space rather than decoded text drastically cuts the compute time and cost required for LLM-driven evolutionary code discovery.

papers.title: Understanding AI from the Inside: The State of Mechanistic Interpretability for AI Safety

summary.tldr: A survey of mechanistic interpretability for AI safety that introduces a unified framework for evaluating claims, synthesizes research methods, and provides hands-on open-source notebooks.
key_points: Surveys core foundational concepts including features, polysemanticity, transformer computation, and circuits.
Reviews techniques for feature extraction, circuit discovery, causal verification, natural language explanations, learning dynamics, and training-data attribution.
Proposes a unified evaluation framework for mechanistic interpretability claims and categorizes six distinct research orientations by goals and trade-offs.
Details practical safety applications including knowledge editing, steering, and monitoring alongside current limitations and failure modes.
Releases a code repository featuring worked examples and reproducible implementations of key surveyed methods.
summary.why_it_matters: It establishes a structured taxonomy and evaluation framework to determine whether understanding internal model mechanics can reliably improve AI control, steering, and safety.

papers.title: StepBack: Step-Level Error-Localized Resampling for Efficient Test-Time Reasoning

summary.tldr: StepBack is a step-level test-time reasoning method that localizes the first error in draft trajectories using lightweight signals and resamples only from that error step forward.
key_points: Identifies likely first-error positions within a small set of draft reasoning trajectories using lightweight signals.
Resamples only the localized error step and its subsequent suffix rather than regenerating entire trajectories.
Applies majority voting to final answers derived from the resampled suffixes.
Matches Self-Consistency accuracy across seven math reasoning and multi-hop QA benchmarks while reducing token consumption by up to 41.26%.
Composes with trajectory-level adaptive inference methods like Adaptive Consistency to further reduce decoding costs.
summary.why_it_matters: It significantly cuts token generation costs and latency for chain-of-thought reasoning without sacrificing task accuracy.

security.title: ARTEX abuse expands as cybercriminals target financial sector

summary.tldr: In October 2026, Cambodia-based threat actor Storm-3358 expanded attacks against the financial sector using the agentic AI offensive framework ARTEX alongside open-source remote access trojans.
key_points: Storm-3358 combined ARTEX with standard tools to scan internet-facing systems, exploit anonymous file upload and SSRF flaws, and achieve lateral movement via WISP, vshell, and AdaptixC2 RATs.

ARTEX agents execute automated attack stages at machine speed, including netcat/curl downloads, API enumeration, web shell persistence, database dumping, password spraying, and cloud identity compromise.
By default, ARTEX relies on tools like Nmap, curl, wget, Python HTTP clients, Norma SDK WebFetch, and Playwright-driven headless Chromium, often leaving default user agent signatures.
Defensive countermeasures tested by Microsoft include Sentinel Deception honeypots, tarpits to exhaust agent time/budget, and fake wins to trigger premature attack termination.
summary.why_it_matters: The deployment of agentic AI frameworks like ARTEX accelerates every stage of the cyber attack lifecycle to machine speed, forcing defenders to adopt AI-driven responses and dynamic deceptive controls.

security.title: Catastrophic Overfitting is Weight Drift the Training Loss Cannot See

summary.tldr: Researchers show catastrophic overfitting in fast adversarial training is caused by invisible weight drift, which can be eliminated by resetting weights to their exponential moving average when validation robustness drops.
key_points: Catastrophic overfitting occurs when single-step training loss remains low while multi-step robustness collapses, as the training objective is blind to the damaging weight drift.
The exponential moving average (EMA) of network weights does not accumulate this drift and retains robustness throughout the overfitting event.
A guard mechanism resets model weights to the EMA upon detecting drops in validation robustness, built on a coupling-based base method that ensures the average remains within the robust region.

The approach eliminated catastrophic overfitting across all test runs and achieved top AutoAttack accuracy among fast methods on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and a third benchmark, beating multi-step references on CIFAR-100 at roughly half the compute cost.
summary.why_it_matters: It provides a computationally efficient fix for catastrophic overfitting in fast adversarial training, enabling robust deep learning models at half the training cost of multi-step methods.

security.title: FedReason: Large Language Models as Weight-Space Meta-Aggregators for Heterogeneous Federated Learning

summary.tldr: FedReason uses an LLM as a zero-shot, weight-space meta-aggregator that generates custom Python aggregation rules every ten rounds by executing server-side analysis code and evaluating candidate rules on a proxy dataset.
key_points: FedReason invokes an LLM (e.g., Claude Opus 5.5) every 10 rounds to inspect client weights inside a restricted server sandbox and output Python aggregation programs, falling back to FedAvg if execution fails.
Client weight tensors remain on the server; the LLM interacts only via printed analysis output and evaluation scores from a 500-image proxy dataset.

Across 12 label-skew runs on CIFAR-10/100 with ResNet-18, FedReason outperformed FedAvg by 1.26 percentage points and beat a proxy-budget matched control selecting among fixed standard rules by 1.08 points.

In Byzantine scenarios with 30% sign-flipping malicious clients, FedReason isolated all attackers in the first round and performed within ~1 percentage point of FLTrust without requiring a root model.
Proxy feedback is critical for stability; removing proxy evaluation caused accuracy to collapse from 73.8% to 38.8% in a tested seed. Average API cost was $0.79 per 60-round run.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that LLMs can dynamically engineer context-aware model aggregation algorithms in code, offering a zero-shot alternative to fixed federated learning rules under heterogeneous and adversarial conditions.

security.title: Escalate or Close: How Fast-Tier Models Handle Held-Out Web Attack Families in Two-Tier Triage

summary.tldr: A study shows supervised fast-tier models in two-tier triage misclassify up to 60% of held-out web attack families as confident benign, whereas zero-shot decision models maintain higher escalation rates but face query-guided evasion.
key_points: Supervised ModernBERT detectors trained on known web attacks give 37% to 60% of held-out path traversal payloads a benign probability below 0.05, escalating only 50% to 81% under a 5% benign budget.
Hosted decision models Jev and Clef escalate at least 97.6% of every held-out attack family within a 5% benign budget, though undisclosed training sets may include these families.
Jev demonstrates high false-positive rates by escalating 37% of benign twin requests and shows inconsistency by re-escalating 60% of previously bypassed requests upon repeated querying.
A search guided by Jev's output probabilities successfully gets 43% of held-out attack payloads past the model within 300 queries.
summary.why_it_matters: Relying on supervised fast-tier models for security triage creates critical blind spots for novel attack vectors, while zero-shot alternatives introduce non-deterministic filtering and susceptibility to query-based evasion.

security.title: AI-Native Task-Oriented Semantic Communications over a Relay: Benefits and Vulnerabilities

summary.tldr: A joint end-to-end task-oriented semantic communication system over a relay node achieves improved image classification and reconstruction at low SNRs, but introduces critical vulnerability to learned Byzantine relay attacks.
key_points: presents a joint end-to-end design optimizing the source encoder, relay transformation, and destination decoders for task accuracy (classification labels) and perceptual image reconstruction.
demonstrates that relay-assisted semantic communication consistently outperforms direct transmission, with performance gains increasing in low SNR regimes.

identifies an insider security risk by formulating a Byzantine attack where the relay applies a learned test-time mapping to inject structured perturbations into intermediate communication representations.
shows that the learned relay attack severely degrades semantic inference accuracy at the destination.
summary.why_it_matters: While relay nodes significantly improve semantic communication performance in low-power or high-noise environments, they introduce severe security vulnerabilities that require targeted defenses against insider Byzantine threats.

security.title: KeHoSu: Keyed Homoglyph Substitution for Authenticated Text Provenance over Copy-Paste Channels

summary.tldr: KeHoSu uses keyed homoglyph substitution to embed traceable platform and user identifiers into text, surviving metadata loss across copy-paste channels without relying on positional state.
key_points: Encodes identifiers comprising a platform field, a user field, and a truncated authentication tag by mapping confusable Unicode code points to individual bits.
Maintains resilience to partial quotations and sentence reordering up to a constant boundary layer by avoiding positional state dependencies.
Characterizes the code-point channel using an achievable region relating its capacity, removability, and detectability.
Preserves embedded marks across 18 common copy-paste platforms, correctly attributing excerpts as short as 167 letters in standard prose and 178 letters in LLM text.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables reliable account-level attribution of redistributed or fragmented text even when platform metadata is completely stripped during manual copy-pasting.

security.title: Dynamic Watermarking and Action-Conditioned Latent Dynamics for Secure Vision-Based Controllers

summary.tldr: An adaptive dynamic-watermarking framework uses an action-conditioned latent dynamics network and a reinforcement learning policy to detect replay attacks in vision-based controllers while minimizing control distortion and safety costs.
key_points: Injects a private Gaussian watermark into the nominal control input to create predictable visual system responses.
Uses a control input-conditioned latent dynamics network (LDN) to predict image-based trajectory evolutions in a compact latent space.
Detects replay attacks by measuring discrepancies between the predicted latent response and the latent embedding of received image observations.
Employs a reinforcement learning policy with a Lagrangian penalty to dynamically adjust watermark covariance, balancing attack detection against safety costs and control distortion.
Validated on a vision-guided UR5 robotic manipulator reaching a target while avoiding a moving human arm under replay attacks.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables secure, real-time detection of visual replay attacks in autonomous control systems without degrading physical tracking performance or violating safety constraints.

security.title: Beyond the Landing Page: Website Blocking, Tracker Visibility, and Human Alignment in Automated Web Crawls

summary.tldr: A study of 2,000 websites demonstrates that LLM-driven agentic crawlers capture significantly more third-party tracker organizations and align better with human browsing than traditional non-agentic crawlers.
key_points: Website denials increase past landing pages for standard automation, but stealth/detection-resistant frameworks mitigate this without inflating tracking data.
On identical URLs, agentic crawlers detect 1.5-1.7 times more third-party tracker organizations than non-agentic crawlers, especially on consent-managed pages.
Agentic crawlers recover 82-87% of tracker organizations observed during human participant visits (n=26), compared to only 58-68% recovered by non-agentic crawlers.
Approximately half of the tracking organizations recorded by agentic crawlers were absent from the human participants' visits.
summary.why_it_matters: Selecting between agentic and traditional crawlers requires balancing trade-offs between stealth, tracker visibility, and true alignment with real human browsing behavior.

security.title: Network Intrusion Forensic Detection System with Explainable Artificial Intelligence and Digital Chain of Custody

summary.tldr: MODEXRE introduces a forensic pipeline integrating a SHA-256 hash-chained chain of custody, OCSF normalization, and SHAP explainability to safely transition validated XGBoost models from laboratory training to formal case inference.
key_points: Architecture features dual modes: a Laboratory mode for training/certifying XGBoost models and a Formal mode for running frozen, hash-verified models on forensic evidence.
Normalizes heterogeneous evidence (Suricata alerts, CEF firewall logs, PCAPs) using the Open Cybersecurity Schema Framework (OCSF).

Corrected a timestamp leak in the Kitsune dataset that initially inflated performance (F1-macro dropped from 0.984 to 0.662) and implemented causal temporal flow aggregation, raising Kitsune multiclass F1-macro to 0.932.

Fixed a certification defect that trained binary classifiers instead of multiclass models; after recertification, real PCAP evaluation shifted from 100% false-malicious flags to 87% Normal classification with Reconnaissance correctly identified.
Achieved F1-macro scores of 0.9538 on a default 4-class CICIDS2017-derived model and 0.6214 on a complex 18-category recertified model.
summary.why_it_matters: It establishes a verifiable bridge between machine learning intrusion detection and legal forensic requirements by ensuring model integrity, cryptographic chain of custody, and explainable predictions.

security.title: Constraint-Aware Evaluation of Reinforcement Learning and Unsupervised Anomaly Detection for Security Operations Alert Triage

summary.tldr: Researchers formalized SOC alert triage as a constrained decision problem and benchmarked offline RL, Isolation Forest, and autoencoders under strict capacity constraints on 74,909 analyst-labeled alerts.
key_points: Formalizes SOC alert triage by incorporating limited analyst capacity, asymmetric error costs, and benign-escalation constraints.
Evaluates three model families using a strict temporal split on 74,909 analyst-labeled production alerts covering 503 unique feature patterns.
At the primary operating point, offline RL achieved the lowest benign-escalation fraction (0.000), outperforming the autoencoder (0.007) and Isolation Forest (0.041).
The evaluated methods prioritized distinct alert clusters, demonstrating complementary coverage rather than redundant triage decisions.
summary.why_it_matters: Constraint-aware evaluation and combining distinct model families allows SOCs to reduce unnecessary alert escalations without exceeding analyst workload limits.

key_points: Reinforcement learning post-training often uses disaggregated GPU clusters to run inference and training in parallel.
The Reshard Collective optimizes the periodic transfer and refitting of updated policy model weights from training GPUs to inference GPUs.
summary.why_it_matters: Efficient weight refitting reduces communication overhead and idle time in disaggregated reinforcement learning infrastructure.

infra.title: SageMaker Inference now supports Multi-Instance GPU to maximize GPU utilization for model endpoints

summary.tldr: Amazon SageMaker Inference now supports NVIDIA Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) partitioning, allowing users to divide a single physical GPU into isolated hardware partitions for independent model deployment.
key_points: Uses NVIDIA MIG to split a physical GPU into up to seven hardware-isolated instances with dedicated compute, cache, memory, and memory bandwidth.
Eliminates cold starts, eviction penalties, and noisy-neighbor latency spikes by offering hardware-enforced fault and tenant isolation.
Integrates via SageMaker inference components, allowing models to request fractional GPU partitions alongside CPU and memory resources.
Incompatible with single-model endpoints, serverless endpoints, and heterogeneous instance pools.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables teams to maximize GPU utilization and reduce hosting costs by deploying multiple fine-tuned or tenant-specific models to a single GPU without compromising security or p99 latency guarantees.

infra.title: Migrating vLLM to the LibTorch Stable ABI

summary.tldr: vLLM migrated its CUDA build and C++ dependencies to the LibTorch Stable ABI as of version 0.33.0, enabling PyTorch upgrades without rebuilding vLLM.
key_points: The LibTorch Stable ABI relies on a three-layer architecture: a C shim exposing selected APIs, C++ wrapper functions, and header-only utilities in torch::headeronly.
Unsupported ops during the migration, such as is_pinned(), were executed in an ABI-stable manner using the general-purpose torch_call_dispatcher C shim to call ATen ops through the dispatcher.
PyTorch added a native stable C++ is_pinned() method in version 2.14 based on feedback from vLLM's migration.
Using the Stable ABI introduces a small amount of additional host-side overhead.
summary.why_it_matters: Users and package distributors can swap or update PyTorch wheels directly without undergoing the time-consuming process of rebuilding and relinking vLLM.

infra.title: Zero Mismatch, Simple Async RL: REINFORCE Zero, DeepSeek-V4.1 and Kimi K3.1

summary.tldr: NVIDIA Research and Inferact introduced REINFORCE Zero, demonstrating that bit-for-bit kernel alignment combined with unclipped importance sampling enables stable asynchronous RL under weight lags up to lag 64.
key_points: Logprob discrepancy in async RL splits into weight lag (log π_θk − log π_θv) and kernel mismatch (log π_θv − log μ_v).
Weight lag changes smoothly over updates and can be corrected with importance sampling (IS), whereas kernel mismatch fluctuates due to batch composition and execution details.
Unclipped importance sampling reweights tokens by π/μ, leveraging exact kernel alignment (zero mismatch) to isolate and eliminate non-deterministic kernel variance.
REINFORCE Zero was demonstrated on DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B, handling weight lags of 2 and 8 on math reasoning, and up to lag 64 on agentic tool use.
summary.why_it_matters: Eliminating kernel mismatch ensures that importance sampling accurately corrects for asynchronous weight lag, preventing training instability in high-throughput off-policy RL.

summary.why_it_matters: Optimizing multi-billion parameter diffusion models on Blackwell GPUs reduces inference latency for real-time visual production and design workflows.
